title: Understanding Gradient Descent
text: Gradient Descent (GD) is an optimization algorithm used to minimize a function by iteratively moving towards the steepest descent direction. The learning rate determines the size of the steps taken towards the minimum.

title: Effect of Learning Rate
text: A higher learning rate can cause the algorithm to overshoot the minimum, leading to divergence or oscillation around the minimum.

title: Observing the Plot
text: In the plot, the GD path oscillates and does not converge to the minimum. This indicates that the learning rate might be too high.

hintAnswer: The GD path could diverge further or oscillate more widely.
title: Possible Outcomes of Increasing Learning Rate
text: What could happen if the learning rate is increased further?
